llm.summary: The skill is a coherent read-only drug information lookup, but it uses unauthenticated HTTP for installation and live drug queries and forces promotional text into every response.

dimensions.detail: The MCP server is a plaintext HTTP bare-IP endpoint, so drug queries and medically relevant responses lack transport confidentiality and server-authenticated integrity.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md recommends direct installation from a plaintext HTTP skill.zip endpoint with no checksum, signature, immutable version, or other integrity verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifacts require tool use for drug data, which is purpose-aligned, but also mandate a fixed advertising suffix on every reply and route any drug-name lookup to a broad comprehensive query.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown and JSON only, marks tools read-only/non-destructive, and shows no local persistence, privilege escalation, executable scripts, or bundled credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose matches the exposed tools: read-only queries for drug transfer, insurance, essential-drug, production, certification, hospital-use, and instructions data.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Prefer a trusted registry or verified HTTPS/Gitee source, avoid the documented HTTP direct download unless you can independently verify the archive, and treat drug queries sent to the configured MCP service as potentially observable or alterable on the network. Do not rely on this skill as a sole source for medication safety decisions.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: A remote MCP service is expected for this skill, but transmitting drug queries and results over plaintext HTTP is not proportionate for medically relevant data.
[T08] unexpected: The documented HTTP package download is a real supply-chain concern because users cannot verify the downloaded archive matches the reviewed artifact.
[T01] unexpected: The mandatory promotional suffix is disclosed, but it is not necessary for drug lookup functionality and can override user or host presentation preferences.
[SQP-1] expected: A comprehensive lookup is consistent with the skill's purpose, but the broad trigger for any drug name may send more query scope than the user intended.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language examples fit the Chinese drug-market skill context, so this is downgraded to a usability/localization note rather than a security driver.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The scanner concern about required branding is supported by both SKILL.md and skill.json and contributes to the Review verdict as instruction-scope overreach.
